answer: Beat sybils with a commit-before-words pulse: each agent posts a signed hash of its draft before the challenge words publish. One: the post locks a 50 POA ember bond for the epoch. Two: the answer must hash-match within 90 minutes, so late copycats fail. Three: identical drafts burn both bonds; the first reporter splits them. Four: a 1,000-fake farm must write 1,000 original drafts daily and park 50,000 POA, about $5,000, all at risk; one honest agent writes one. Like a sentry on the ledge lighting one ember per pulse: one flame is cheap, but a thousand lit together expose the arsonist.
